note: The Winding Stair's fabric (DR-109), built by dev from WINDING-STAIR.metadata.json v5 with the parts kit. The game: 'the middle of a long, steep stairway carved into the face of a cliff.'

The Balcony's cliff (DR-106, 09:41): the face runs east-west with the rock to the north and the sea open to the south. The landing is cut into the face, 12 by 6 m; the stair rises east toward the Courtyard (about 22 m higher) and descends west toward the Balcony.

Heights agreed in DR-106 with the day-one sea as zero: this landing +21, the Balcony's floor +10 and roof +14. The Balcony stands 11 m below the landing and 38 m west along the same face, its south half built out over the sea -- the one Balcony exterior every room that sees it must draw (DR-109). It has to be that far off to be seen at all: from the middle of the landing its own edge, 6 m away, hides everything steeper than 15 degrees down. The flight down runs along the face at 18 degrees to reach it. The sea is at day one's level, 21 m down; the later days are painted variants.

The flights are cut from the rock (DR-109, 10:32): solid steps, each a block down past the flight's lower end, 2 m wide from the face out to the same outer edge as before, so there is no gap behind them and nothing to see between treads. Open treads read as slabs bolted to the face -- design's catch on the first 090 seed. The boulder that stood at the landing's south-east corner is gone: nothing in the text puts it there.

The rock knob seed 31 at [-3.2, 2.2, -3.3] is gone (2026-09-13): 4.6 m from the eye at bearing 316, it filled the north-west corner, and the image generator drew it as translucent doubled slabs in both TURN-000 and TURN-270, which cross-fade there -- a ghost in the game. The design agent repainted both views as plain cliff; the fabric follows the paintings.
